definitions.explanation: A substance that produces a pleasant aroma when burned, used in religious ceremonies, meditation, and traditional Japanese culture.
A pleasant smell, especially from natural sources such as flowers, herbs, or wood.

examples.japanese: {仏壇|ぶつだん}の{前|まえ}で{香|こう}を{焚|た}いた。
examples.english: I burned incense in front of the Buddhist altar.

examples.japanese: {寺|てら}に{入|はい}ると、{香|こう}の{煙|けむり}がゆっくりと{漂|ただよ}っていた。
examples.english: When I entered the temple, incense smoke was slowly drifting through the air.

examples.japanese: {白檀|びゃくだん}の{香|こう}が{部屋|へや}に{広|ひろ}がった。
examples.english: The fragrance of sandalwood spread through the room.

examples.japanese: {梅|うめ}の{香|こう}に{誘|さそ}われて、{庭|にわ}に{出|で}た。
examples.english: Drawn by the scent of plum blossoms, I went out into the garden.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 refers to the physical incense product and the act of burning it. Sense 2 is a literary or refined way to refer to pleasant scents, especially from nature. In everyday conversation, {匂|にお}い or {香|かお}り is more common for general smells and fragrances.

CULTURAL NOTE:
{香道|こうどう} (the way of incense) is one of the three classical Japanese arts of refinement, alongside {茶道|さどう} (tea ceremony) and {華道|かどう} (flower arrangement).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {香|こう}を{焚|た}く (to burn incense)
- {香|こう}の{煙|けむり} (incense smoke)
- {線香|せんこう} (incense stick)
- {香道|こうどう} (the art of incense appreciation)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {香|かお}り: fragrance, aroma — the more common everyday word for pleasant scents
- {匂|にお}い: smell, scent — neutral term for any smell, pleasant or not
